statement.text:
Can some or all groups of the following sorts be written as homomorphic
images of nonprincipal ultraproducts of countable families of groups? This is Ques-
tion 18 in (G. M. Bergman, Pacific J. Math., 274 (2015) 451–495).
   (a) Infinite finitely generated groups of finite exponent.
   (b) For an infinite set X, the group of those permutations of X that move only
finitely many elements.
    It is known that no group of permutations containing an element with exactly one
infinite orbit can be written as an image of such an ultraproduct (ibid.).
                                                                             G. M. Bergman
